purpose: Route stable build and runtime error signatures to the smallest relevant HarmonyOS KMP knowledge set. A match proposes checks; it never proves the root cause or a successful fix.

evidence_policy.rule: Never promote demo source, object construction, HTTP-only traffic, or swallowed exceptions to compile/device/runtime proof.

patterns: tls sessions are not supported on native platform
tls not available in native platform
tls is not supported on native platform
likely_causes: A CIO-backed client reached HTTPS on Kotlin/Native without a supported TLS session implementation.
The intended ohosArm64 engine dependency or platform actual was not selected by production wiring.
checks: Trace the production HttpClient constructor and record the engine class selected on ohosArm64.
Keep engine dependencies in target source sets and resolve their exact Foundation coordinates.
Confirm ohos.permission.INTERNET, DNS/VPN reachability, and the final packaged native libraries separately.
Run a physical-device https:// request and assert expected status/body; client creation or plain HTTP is insufficient.

likely_causes: Harmony manifest permission, DNS, VPN/proxy routing, or device connectivity is unavailable.
A network error was misclassified as proof that the selected client/engine works.
checks: Inspect module.json5 for ohos.permission.INTERNET and any capability-specific permission.
Verify the same host through the device network/VPN route before changing library code.
Keep DNS/permission/transport/TLS failures distinct in result state and evidence.

likely_causes: SQLDelight's global native linker option added a redundant system -lsqlite3 lookup to the ohosArm64 link.
checks: Use the cookbook's linkSqlite configuration for an OHOS-bearing module.
Run the final shared-library link task and inspect symbols/needed libraries; compileKotlin is insufficient.
Reject dummy archives and migration-authored SQLite search paths.

likely_causes: The database used a relative/non-writable path or the Harmony private directory was not supplied through the platform boundary.
checks: Obtain the writable application directory from the Harmony host and keep directory/basePath separate from the database filename.
Verify parent directory creation and file access on the physical device.
Close and reopen the database, then restart the app; an in-memory fallback is not persistence proof.

patterns: there are multiple datastores active for the same file
multiple datastore instances are active for the same file
file is already locked by datastore
likely_causes: More than one DataStore instance or scope owns the same file.
The store was created before the Harmony host supplied its application-private files directory.
checks: Initialize the files directory at Ability startup before first store access.
Create one process-level DataStore instance per file with one owned SupervisorJob scope.
Verify persistence after app restart and reject silent temporary-directory fallback.
